key_insight: DP-SPA preserves continual LoRA performance under differential privacy by separating learned updates into a stable subspace for retention and a plastic subspace for new-task adaptation.
engineering_relevance: For privacy-sensitive engineering models, this offers a practical way to update pretrained systems across tasks while reducing forgetting and avoiding privacy-induced degradation in adaptation.
method: Build a stable subspace from previously privatized updates.
Define a plastic subspace in the orthogonal complement of pretrained weights.
Privately optimize only one LoRA factor per step and recalibrate stable coefficients using historical/current update energy before merging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five datasets, eight settings, and multiple privacy budgets, with improved average accuracy and reduced forgetting over baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly estimating and maintaining the stable/plastic subspace structure, which may add implementation complexity and sensitivity to subspace quality.
paper_title: Stable-Plastic Subspace Construction for Differentially Private Continual LoRA
